In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the silicate glass is the primary cause for microstructural degradation of anode/electroyte interfaces and Ni/YSz grain boundaries in SOFC.
the microstructural and phase degradation of the anode/eletrolyte interface are mainly caused by the impurity phases (silicate and Ni 2 P) in the anode.
the microstructure degradation of the anode/electricity interface in SOFC is a result of both the chemical reactions and mechanical stresses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FIB/lift out techniques have been successfully applied to prepare TEM specimens from SOFC anode/electroltye interfaces and to analyze the microstructural degradation in the interfacially region.

the microstructural degradation is caused by the accumulation of silicate glass phase at the anode/elelctrolyte interface, which is a consequence of a reaction between YSZ and the impurities in the anode.
the silicate glass is a product of the anode/electricity interface reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the silicate glass phase can be detrimental to the long-term operation of SOFC.
the silicate glass formed at the interface is a key factor for the microstructural degradation and the failure of the anode/electric interface.
the impurity phase is not the main cause for microstructural degradation of an SOFC interface, but rather the NiO reduction process is the main culprit.
